_tables: Parser tables (.data, read by both sides) rewired: state 0 shifts token 0 (lexer's first return) to state 1; states 1-6 have no shift (action list starts negative), so each reduces its default rule (parseDefaultRules[s], set per case), whose goto (parseRuleGotos[rule] = 0/2/4/6, set per case) leads to state 2/3/4/5. A case puts rule R1..Rn in states 1..n and rule 0 (accept) in state n+1; rule lengths are set to 1, so every rule of a chain sees the same top. A lexer returning 1 skips the shift: state 0 reduces parseDefaultRules[0] directly (top[0] is then the zeroed initial slot). The stacks are allocated at +0x100/+0x200 into their objects so the slots under top are case data: with the shift, top[0] = parser+0xc, top[-1] = valueStack+0x210 (zeroed by the first push), top[-k] = valueStack+0x220-0x10k; without it top[-k] = valueStack+0x210-0x10k.
_lists: The list helpers (0x1002dd0f/dd6f/dc37/dd34/dce0/dcfd/db83/dbdd) are stubs: a passthrough's own calls run unstubbed, into the real allocator. Their list arg is often a local of the frame, so it is not recorded. Rules 3, 9, 0xb and 0xd leave &local in the value stack (a frame address, different on each side), so those cases chain rule 0x99 after them, which overwrites that word with 1.

cases._r: chain 3, 0x99: frame count matches (0x99 overwrites the &local result)
